'''Minami Shingū-sha''' (南新宮社) is a Shinto shrine located in Atsuta Ward, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the Sessha (subsidiary shrines) within Atsuta Shrine.

== deity ==
The enshrined deity is '''Susanoo-no-Mikoto''' (スサノオノミコト).<ref name="HP Minami Shingū-sha">[https://atsutajingu.or.jp/jingu/about/keidai/36.html Minami Shingū-sha | Atsuta Shrine Official Site] (Accessed June 28, 2018)</ref>

In pre-modern times, the shrine was known for enshrining '''Gozu Tennō''' (ごずてんのう), a deity syncretized with Susanoo and regarded as an Epidemic deity.{{#tag:ref|''"Minami Shingū is Gozu Tennō itself."'' (''Atsuta Daijingū Shintai Den''){{Sfn|Engi Yuiisho-hen|2002|p=159}}|group="Note"}} The shrine is believed to have been established as a Gion Shrine (present-day Yasaka Shrine).{{#tag:ref|''"Gozu Tennō was enshrined here, and it was said to be a shrine associated with Gion."'' (''Atsumi-sō''){{Sfn|Atsumi-sō|1911|p=31}}|group="Note"}} It was also commonly referred to as ''Tennō-sha'' (天王社).{{#tag:ref|Mentioned in ''Atsumi-sō''{{Sfn|Atsumi-sō|1911|p=31}} and ''Atsuta Honsha Massha Shintai Sonmeiki''{{Sfn|Engi Yuiisho-zokuhen1|2005|p=66}}|group="Note"}} Some theories suggest it was a branch shrine of Tsushima Shrine,{{Sfn|Shinshū City History 2|1998|p=446}} a major shrine of the Tsushima Faith. The associated Honji Suijaku deity was Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha.{{Sfn|Engi Yuiisho-hen|2002|p=159}}

== History ==
The founding date is uncertain, with some records suggesting 1000 (Chōhō 2) or 1023 (Jian 3).{{#tag:ref|''Atsuta Daijingū Shintai Den Monogatarigaki''{{Sfn|Engi Yuiisho-zokuhen1|2005|p=179}}|group="Note"}} During the reign of Emperor Ichijō, Japan experienced a severe epidemic, and in Kyoto, a Goryō-e was held in 1001.{{#tag:ref|''"On the 9th day of the 5th month, a ritual was held at Shinano to pacify the epidemic deity. It was called Goryō-e."''
(''Nihon Kiryaku,'' later Ichijō Tennō section){{Sfn|Kokushi Taikei 5|1897|pp=1046-1047}}|group="Note"}} It is believed that Minami Shingū-sha was established in response to this epidemic crisis.{{#tag:ref|''"In the third year of Jian (1023), an epidemic spread nationwide, so it was enshrined for pacification."''
(''Shaden''){{Sfn|Engi Yuiisho-zokuhen1|2005|p=245}}|group="Note"}} However, little is known about the shrine's activities during the Heian period and Kamakura period.

The shrine was reconstructed in 1291 (Shōō 4),{{Sfn|City History: Shrines and Temples|1915|p=161}} and a document from 1431 (Eikyō 3) mentions "Minami Shingū."{{Sfn|Fukada|1898|p=18}} Some scholars theorize that Minami Shingū-sha did not exist until the mid-Muromachi period, and that it was originally the site of Magowaka Mikoshi Shrine, which was later replaced by Minami Shingū-sha under the patronage of the Oda clan, who were devout worshippers of Gozu Tennō.{{Sfn|Tsuda|1916|p=71}}

Despite being a subsidiary shrine of Atsuta Shrine, Minami Shingū-sha had a unique role as a deity of epidemics and was a major center for popular Gion faith and Tsushima Faith. It was also the local Ujigami for the merchants and commoners of Atsuta.{{Sfn|Historic Sites and Cultural Properties|1991|p=70}}

In 1686 (Jōkyō 3), during a major restoration of Atsuta Shrine under the supervision of Sakai Tadaakira, doubts were raised about the legitimacy of Minami Shingū-sha. However, the shrine's existence was defended by Atsuta Shrine officials who described it as an important "divine mystery" (神秘).{{#tag:ref|''"Minami Shingū is a shrine of special divine mystery."''
(''Atsuta Miya Gozoei Jōkyōki''){{Sfn|Zōei Senkū-hen Jō|1980|p=195}}|group="Note"}}
